subject: Private deployment: network & streaming performance check - FinLytics follow-up
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir@finlytics.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-11T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Private deploy — initial perf asks and topology

Hi Ava,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. Per our internal perf owners, here's a compact summary of our requirements and the pieces we need help validating:

- Desired SLOs (goal):
  - 99th percentile response latency <= 150 ms for prompt sizes <= 256 tokens (server-side generation, non-streaming).
  - Streaming tail (time-to-first-byte and inter-token jitter) target <= 200 ms for models that stream incremental tokens.
  - Sustained throughput: baseline 120 requests/sec with average 1.5k tokens produced (burst to 250 rps).
  - Concurrency: support 100 concurrent long-lived streaming sessions (typical session = 20s).

- Network/infra constraints:
  - Private deployment inside our VPC (AWS us-east-2). We plan to peer/attach via Transit Gateway; we can provide TGW attachments and route tables.
  - Egress must go through our NAT with static IPs (we will provide NAT IP ranges).
  - No persistent logs exported off-prem beyond minimal metadata (per compliance).
  - We need evidence of packet loss/jitter tolerance & a fallback plan if peering shows elevated RTT.

- Tests we want to run with Redwood before committing: traceroutes, iperf3 runs (1 min steady-state), simulated streaming run (100 concurrent clients, 2k token backlog) to measure tail latency, RPS ramp.

Attached is our simplified infra diagram (finlytics-infrastructure-topology.pdf).

Next steps we propose:
1) Redwood provides a recommended test checklist and IP ranges to allow our networking team to open routes.
2) Align on a 2-hour test window next week for a live streaming run.
3) Redwood shares a concise SLO-to-infra mapping (what instance types, expected tokens/sec, and pre-warm guidance).

Can you confirm availability for a test window and what we should expect on Redwood's side (public IPs, collector ports, monitoring hooks)?

Thanks — Samir

--
Samir Rao
Head of Infrastructure, FinLytics
cloudops@finlytics.com

Samir — thanks for the clear summary and the diagram, very helpful.

A few quick confirmations and action items from Redwood to unblock the test:

Action items (Redwood):
- We will provide the list of Redwood egress IPs and ports by EOD tomorrow so your TGW team can create route/NAT exceptions.
- We'll publish a short test checklist (iperf3 settings, recommended packet sizes, streaming harness config) and a playbook for interpreting results (expected jitter/loss thresholds).
- For the streaming run, Redwood will bring a canary fleet sized to your concurrency target and a fallback capacity plan (we can move traffic to a dedicated reserved pool if the peering latency is high).
- We will share a monitoring dashboard link (read-only) with tokenized access for the run and provide trace logs that do not include prompt content.

Initial technical notes:
- From experience, for 99p <= 150 ms on short prompts we typically aim for intra-region RTT < 25–30 ms and packet loss < 0.1% during steady-state. If RTT looks like 50–80 ms we'll recommend colocating a smaller dedicated pool in your region or using our Dedicated capacity with pre-warmed nodes.
- For streaming tails we tune our gRPC windowing and KV cache locality; the streaming harness will show inter-token jitter and time-to-first-byte.

Proposed test window options (2-hour blocks):
- Tue 2027-04-13 09:00–11:00 ET
- Wed 2027-04-14 14:00–16:00 ET

Please confirm which slot works and provide the TGW attachment ID and NAT IPs.

Also copying Karthik and Marcus for SLO mapping and instance recommendations.

Best,
Ava Chen

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-04-12T08:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy — initial perf asks and topology

Hi all — adding the SLO->infra mapping and pragmatic tuning notes so FinLytics can plan capacity. Attachment: redwood-slo-mapping.xlsx

Summary (short):
- For the stated targets (120 rps, 1.5k tokens produced average, 100 concurrent streams):
  - Recommended instance profile: 4x A40-like GPUs (quantized LLM path) or 2x A100-80GB for higher single-stream throughput.
  - Expected tokens/sec per GPU (conservative): 350–500 tps depending on quantization and model; plan capacity for 250 tps to include headroom.
  - KV cache locality: enable sticky routing for long-lived streams to keep cache hot; that reduces per-token latency by ~20–30% in practice.

Network expectations we use for acceptance:
- Baseline RTT (Redwood edge -> your TGW) < 35 ms for target SLO. If 35–60 ms, we can still meet targets with dedicated pool + higher replication factor.
- Packet loss < 0.2% across a 5-minute steady-state iperf run; jitter < 3 ms.
- Egress NAT: confirm stable IPs; we need a /28 or equivalent to whitelist to avoid ephemeral changes during test.

Operational toggles during the run:
- Batching window: adjust between 20–40 ms to trade latency for throughput during bursts.
- Streaming window: enable aggressive pre-fetch for first 3 tokens to improve time-to-first-byte when jitter is seen.

I'll be available during the test window to tweak instance counts and streaming knobs. Marcus will monitor traces and latency heatmaps.

Karthik
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai

- No application payload (prompts/outputs) may leave our VPC; logs must be limited to request/response metadata and anonymized traces.

I attached an updated network diagram (network-topology-v2.pdf) with the TGW details. If you can confirm the Redwood egress list tomorrow we will finalize the firewall entries.

On the demo: we'd like to run the 100 concurrent streaming client test for 20 minutes, then a 10-minute burst to 250 rps, and finally a 15-minute steady-state iperf run measuring packet loss/jitter. Please include expected dashboards in the run plan.

Appreciate the quick turnaround,
Samir
